value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 1
variable_description: The finest ASGS area the taxpayer's address geocodes to on the return, at the 2021 boundaries. SA1s hold a few hundred people each, so this is the level at which a tax record says something about a neighbourhood rather than a suburb, and it is what SA2, SA3, SA4 and the state code on the same row roll up from. Because it is derived from the address, it inherits whatever the address is: a postal address or an agent's office puts the taxpayer in the wrong SA1 entirely.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. There are 61,845 SA1s, of which 34 are special purpose codes for migratory, offshore and no-usual-address records.
limitation: SA1 counts are small enough that a cell can identify people, which is why tax analysis at this level is normally aggregated before release. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions, so an SA1 series across the change needs a correspondence rather than a join.
rationale: The field is an SA1 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA1 definition, its design population and its special purpose codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code.' with no value domain, so nothing said how fine the area is or that it is derived from an address that may not be a residence.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 2
variable_description: The taxpayer's SA2 at the 2021 boundaries, which is the ASGS level most tax analysis is published at. SA2s are built to represent communities that interact socially and economically, so they answer questions about a suburb or town where the SA1 below them is too small to release and the SA3 above them is too coarse to recognise. It is derived from the same geocoded address as the other geography columns on the row.
value_definition: A nine-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. There are 2,473 SA2s, of which 19 are special purpose codes, with populations generally between 3,000 and 25,000.
limitation: An SA2 is a statistical area, not a suburb: its boundaries follow population rather than local names, so an SA2 and the suburb it is named after are not the same place. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions, so a series across the change needs a correspondence.
rationale: The field is an SA2 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA2 definition, its design population and its special purpose codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code.' with no value domain.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 3
variable_description: The taxpayer's SA3 at the 2021 boundaries, a regional grouping of SA2s. SA3s are designed around labour markets and regional service catchments, which makes this the natural level for questions about where people work and what a regional economy looks like, rather than where a particular street is. It is derived from the same geocoded address as the finer geography on the row.
value_definition: A five-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. SA3s generally hold between 30,000 and 130,000 people.
limitation: An SA3 aggregates communities that differ from one another, so a median or a rate at this level hides variation the SA2 column would show. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions.
rationale: The field is an SA3 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA3 definition and its design population.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 3 code.' with no value domain.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Areas Level 4
variable_description: The taxpayer's SA4 at the 2021 boundaries, the largest sub-state ASGS area. SA4s are built to be big enough for the Labour Force Survey to publish at, which is why labour market comparisons are made here and why an SA4 is the level at which a tax measure can be set beside an unemployment rate. It is derived from the same geocoded address as the finer geography on the row.
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS 2021 code whose leading digit is the state. There are 108 SA4s, of which 19 are special purpose codes, generally holding 100,000 to 500,000 people.
limitation: An SA4 covers a whole city sector or a large slice of a state, so it cannot answer anything local; the SA2 column is the one for that. Boundaries changed between the 2016 and 2021 editions.
rationale: The field is an SA4 code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the SA4 definition, its design population and that it is the level the Labour Force Survey publishes at.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code.' with no value domain.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the taxpayer's address falls in, at the 2024 boundaries. Unlike the SA codes beside it this is an administrative boundary rather than a statistical one: it is drawn by state legislation and changes when councils amalgamate or split, so it is the right column for anything involving council rates, local government policy or a comparison with council-published data.
value_definition: A five-digit ABS-assigned code for the LGA, whose leading digit is the state. The ABS approximates LGA boundaries from mesh blocks, so the coded area is a close fit to the gazetted boundary rather than the boundary itself.
limitation: LGAs vary enormously in size and population, from a few hundred people to more than a million, so a per-LGA average is not comparable across them the way an SA3 average is. Amalgamations break the series: an LGA that merged has no continuous history, and the 2024 vintage cannot be joined to an earlier one by code.
rationale: The field is an LGA code at the 2024 vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes how it approximates LGA boundaries from mesh blocks and that LGAs are a non-ABS structure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2024 Local Government Area code.' with no value domain, and nothing said the boundary is administrative rather than statistical.

value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, States and Territories
variable_description: The state or territory the taxpayer's address falls in, at the 2021 boundaries. It is the coarsest of the geography columns on the row and the one that survives every boundary revision, which makes it the safe level for a long series where the SA codes below it change between editions. It is also the leading digit of every other ASGS code on the row, so a disagreement between them is a data problem rather than a real difference.
value_definition: A single digit, 1 to 8 for the states and territories in ABS order and 9 for other territories, with a further code for migratory, offshore and no-usual-address records.
limitation: State of address is not state of economic activity: someone living near a border, or working in one state and living in another, is counted where they live. The code says nothing about metropolitan against regional, which the SA4 or the remoteness columns carry.
rationale: The field is a state code at the 2021 ASGS vintage on the income tax return tables. The ABS publishes the state and territory codes and their order.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the one-line curated description '2021 state or territory code.' with no value domain.
